newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END UP BUT STILL TOP-HEAVY.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END UP BUT STILL TOP-HEAVY.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended firmer but off their highs on Tuesday as the market ran out of energy on the upside, dealers said.

The dollar's firm grip above 115 yen throughout the Asian session and Wall Street's slight recovery overnight kept the market well supported but gains were limited by a lack of fresh buying incentives.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended 270 points higher at 19,120, after briefly rising to 19,250.
"The short-term outlook is still very soft. If it keeps staying below 19,250 on the close, the next objective would be near 18,000," a trader at a local futures house said.
He said the September Nikkei now faced a stiff barrier around the 19,400-19,500 region.
Taiwan stock index futures ended lower in line with broad profit-taking in Taipei shares. The August MSCI contract lost 4.9 points to end at 413.4 on volume of 2,389 lots.
